checks: Verified source a2bca99efffd5fb9 §§1–2 (1)–(4) and its exact restricted support. The draft uses the accepted dependence theorem for h(P′) rather than the source's alternative explicit eight-deletion witness.

The original complete lattice hull contains conv(W). Of the two sites outside W, p₉ is strictly separated by b+c, while p₂ lies in conv(W) via both disjoint midpoint pairs. The nine exposing normals show each W point is a vertex. The rank-three base determinant and rank-four lift determinant both have absolute value one in the selected coordinates.

The supporting face b=0 contains precisely the four retained corners and the center among integer sites, since every original site has b≥0. The midpoint intersection is interior in that two-dimensional face. Thus there is exactly one nonvertex site. Restriction of the anchored height identities is exact, and g₂=1/2 is the only discarded height.

The predecessor proves the same lifted W hull has exactly its nine vertices as its integer trace. Its nine deletion hulls miss this set jointly, while removing any one hull leaves the lift of that hull's deleted index in all the others. The one-excluding-set-per-site bound gives h(T′)≤9 for all finite families of convex sets.

The only nonsingleton minimal-face hyperedge in P′ is the five-point diamond, so the accepted decomposition adds h(D) and five ones. Four corners are not empty relative to D because they enclose its center. Any four-point subset containing the center includes three corners and hence an opposite pair, violating convex position. The five-point set also fails convex position. The accepted empty-vertex upper lemma gives h(D)≤3. Three noncollinear corners have deletion segments meeting pairwise and missing in triple intersection, proving h(D)≥3.

Every retained lift is a vertex, so its dependence component is a singleton. The four former corners therefore contribute four instead of the original component contribution three. As a direct independent check of the lower h(P′) certificate, take W without p₃. The missing p₃ lies outside its hull by the b=0 face and c≤1 there. Deleting p₀ as well leaves p₁,p₆ on that face, whose segment excludes p₂. The other eight points are excluded by their own exposing deletion.
